newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices flat to up after APIs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices flat to up after APIs.

text.p: U.S. crude oil futures edged higher Wednesday in overnight ACCESS trade, buoyed by an inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) which showed shrinking stocks last week, traders said.
In a delayed report sent Wednesday, API reported U.S. crude oil inventories dropped 3.42 million barrels to 286.04 barrels for the week ended January 17.
The March NYMEX contract rose eight cents a barrel to $24.32 during after-hours trade, but brokers said profit-taking would continue to pressure the contract down this week.
"All the bullish news has been factored into prices," a trader said, noting cold weather in the northeastern U.S. has failed to boost crude values signficantly.
ACCESS activity stood at 921 lots traded in March and 1,194 overall.
Traders saw support tested early Thursday around $23.30 to $23.40 a barrel.
NYMEX February heating oil rose 0.21 cents a gallon to 67.10 cents a gallon, with about 69 lots traded in the front month and 118 traded overall.
Prices were driven higher by a decrease in distillates -- ncluding "heat" -- which fell 2.9 million barrels, according to the API.
Gasoline futures were steady at 66.89 cents a gallon, with 37 lots traded in the nearby month and 48 exchanged overall.
Gasoline futures prices rose about 3 million barrels last week.
